entries.expected_region: as described in original LabelCritic prompt
entries.ct_appearance: Consider the following questions, were positive answers indicate a correct annotation: Point 1: Does the red shape resemble a line? It does not matter if the line is curved or straight. Also, the line may have a round bulge at the top, representing the aortic arch (upper chest).Point 2: Is the red shape a single connected part? If you see two or more red shapes in the image, it is wrong.
entries.shape_and_continuity_prior: tubular or branching vascular structure following an anatomically plausible course; it should be continuous in projection unless naturally branching or partially outside the field of view
anatomical_constraints: Consider the following questions, were positive answers indicate a correct annotation: Point 1: Does the red shape resemble a line? It does not matter if the line is curved or straight. Also, the line may have a round bulge at the top, representing the aortic arch (upper chest).Point 2: Is the red shape a single connected part? If you see two or more red shapes in the image, it is wrong.
Use AP-like CT projection orientation when judging overlay location.
common_failure_modes: mask leaks into adjacent organs or unrelated structures
mask is made of many scattered disconnected blobs when a coherent structure is expected
mask is far outside the expected body region or outside the CT field of view
mask volume is implausibly large or small relative to the target and candidate alternatives
mask follows a neighboring structure with a similar appearance rather than the requested target
rejection_rules: Reject or downgrade a candidate if it clearly segments a different organ or wrong side.
Reject or downgrade a candidate if most foreground lies outside the expected region or parent structure.
Reject or downgrade a candidate if the overlay is dominated by scattered false-positive islands.
Prefer the candidate with the most anatomically plausible location, continuity, boundary, and relation to landmarks, not the one with the largest area.
For tubular/vascular structures, prefer anatomically continuous or branching candidates; penalize broken, random, or over-expanded masks.
